{{Five kings of Wa}}'''San of Wa''' (讃) was a king of [[Wa (name of Japan)|Wa]] in the first half of the [[5th century]] (middle of the [[Kofun period|Kofun era]]).{{Sfn|倭王讃（日本人名大辞典）}}

He was the brother of [[Chin of Wa|Chin]], the first of the "[[Five kings of Wa]]" (although San is not seen as a king in the historical record{{Sfn|倭王讃（朝日日本歴史人物事典）}}). Some have compared him to either the 15th [[Emperor Ōjin|Emperor Ojin]], the 16th [[Emperor Nintoku]], or the 17th [[Emperor Richū|Emperor Richu]].

== Records ==
=== Book of Song ===
; [[Book of Song|Song Book]], Chronicles
In the [[Book of Song]], the [[Emperor Wu of Song]] issued an imperial decree in the 2nd year of Yongchou ([[421]]), ordering the [[Liu Song dynasty]] to grant [[Emperor Wu of Song|Wu of Song]] a title for his tribute from Wanli.<ref name="東洋文庫 宋書"/><ref name="講談社 宋書"/>
: In the 2nd year of Yuanjia ([[425]]), San also sent Cao Da, a librarian, to the Song dynasty to present a written appeal to [[Emperor Wen of Song|Wen]], and presented him with local specialties. Later, after San's death, his younger brother Jin stood as king.<ref name="東洋文庫 宋書">『東アジア民族史 1 正史東夷伝（[[東洋文庫 (平凡社)|東洋文庫]]264）』 平凡社、1974年、pp. 309-313</ref><ref name="講談社 宋書">『倭国伝 中国正史に描かれた日本（[[講談社学術文庫]]2010）』 講談社、2010年、pp. 117-123</ref>
; The Book of Song (Song shu), Book of the Chronicles (Song shu), Book of the Chronicles (Song shu)
: The Wen Di Ji, Yuan Jia 7 ([[430|430 years]]), Sho Tsuki article states that the king of Japan sent an envoy to present a fang material (a san or jin envoy?).

=== Book of Liang ===
In the [[Book of Liang]], the article on Japan states that there was a "tribute" to the king of Japan when [[Emperor An of Jin]] of the Jin ([[Eastern Jin]]), and that when An died, his younger brother Ya stood up.<ref name="東洋文庫 梁書">『東アジア民族史 1 正史東夷伝（東洋文庫264）』 平凡社、1974年、pp. 315-319</ref>

=== History of the Southern Dynasties ===
In the article of [[History of the Southern Dynasties]], the Japanese envoys and tributes during the reign of Emperor An of the Jin dynasty and the contents of the Song Book of Biography are described.

=== Others ===
According to the article in the [[Book of Jin]], in the 9th year of the reign of Emperor An ([[413]]), Goguryeo and Japan sent an envoy to offer a variety of goods (one theory is that it was an envoy from the Emperor Hsin). In the "[[Taiping Yulan]]" an anecdote in the "Ukihee Kiyoi Note" states that the tribute included "a ginseng and other items offered by the Japanese government.{{Sfn|倭の五王（国史）}}{{Sfn|森公章|2010|pp=7-11}}
